q-112198.name: Question 1
q-112198.problem:
Find the vector $x$, if $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ and 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$
q-112198.worked_solution:
We know that any vector in  $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,B.$ Since we are told that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -4\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={{(\,8\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{{(\,-4\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}32 \\ -24 \\ -16\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-36 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -20 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the vector x, if B={b1,b2} is a basis of Span{b1,b2}, and b1=[4−3−2],b2=[9−1−1],[x]B=[8−4].

EXPLANATION

We know that any vector in Span{b1,b2} has the form

x1[4−3−2]+x2[9−1−1]

where x1 and x2 are the coordinates relative to the basis B. Since we are told that [x]B=[8−4], we obtain

x=(8)⏟x1[4−3−2]+(−4)⏟x2[9−1−1]=[32−24−16]+[−3644]=[−4−20−12].

q-34718.name: Question 2
q-34718.problem:
Find the vector $x$, if $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ and  

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
q-34718.worked_solution:
We know that any vector in  $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ has the form 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,B.$ Since we are told that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={{(\,3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{{(\,2\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3 \\ 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-112197.name: Question 3
q-112197.problem:
Find the vector $x$, if $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ and 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -7\end{aligned}].
$$
q-112197.worked_solution:
We know that any vector in  $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,B.$ Since we are told that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -7\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={{(\,6\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{{(\,-7\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -30 \\ -18\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ 21 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -9 \\ -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the vector x, if B={b1,b2} is a basis of Span{b1,b2}, and b1=[1−5−3],b2=[2−3−1],[x]B=[6−7].

a
[8−9−1]
b
[−8−9−11]
c
[11−9−1]

[−2−311]
e
[93−11]
Submit

EXPLANATION

We know that any vector in Span{b1,b2} has the form

x1[1−5−3]+x2[2−3−1]

where x1 and x2 are the coordinates relative to the basis B. Since we are told that [x]B=[6−7], we obtain

x=(6)⏟x1[1−5−3]+(−7)⏟x2[2−3−1]=[6−30−18]+[−14217]=[−8−9−11].

q-75958.name: Question 4
q-75958.problem:
Find the vector $x$, if $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ and 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\end{aligned}].
$$
q-75958.worked_solution:
We know that any vector in  $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,B.$ Since we are told that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={{(\,3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+{{(\,7\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]= \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -15\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}14 \\ -14 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -14 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-34760.problem:
Find the vector $x$, if $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ and 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -\frac{8}{3} \\ 12\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 10 \\ 18\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$
q-34760.worked_solution:
We know that any vector in  $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -\frac{8}{3} \\ 12\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 10 \\ 18\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,B.$ Since we are told that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} \\ -3\end{aligned}],$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={{(\frac{3}{2})}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -\frac{8}{3} \\ 12\end{aligned}]+{{(-3)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 10 \\ 18\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -4 \\ 18\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-18 \\ -30 \\ -54\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -34 \\ -36\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-75845.name: Question 6
q-75845.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\},$ where 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}?$
q-75845.worked_solution:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that 

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={{(\,1\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{1}}+{{(\,0\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{2}}+{{(\,-3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{3}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{3}}
$$

which means that

$$
x=1\cdot {b}_{1}+0\cdot {b}_{2}+(-3)\cdot {b}_{3}
$$

and therefore

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}],
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}=1.$
